scope: scripts/qualify_operation_status.py with the Host of a frozen Debug build of 99a3709 (D:\wp\sr04), 136 steps and 51 clean Host lifetimes, over copies of the durable operation and admission stores retained by 18 curated native runs: the twelve watch runs of local.watch.native.20261028 (eight worker-loss points, three Host-loss points, one uninterrupted), author3 and exact1 of local.watch.authoring.20261028, and the alarm and hardware runs local.alarm_imports.20261028, local.hardware_changes.20261028 and local.alarm_text_list.20261028. For each copy: engineering_operation_status returns every operation (prepared, reconciled, stopped) and admission (change_apply, change_restore, scratch_create, watch_fixture_seed, watch_authoring_source_negative) exactly as its newest on-disk revision; the 14 status reads the native runs recorded live, including outcomeUnknown reads right after worker loss, equal the on-disk revision of the same number; retained admission responses match their SHA-256 and none is unresolved; an unknown ID refuses as OperationNotFound and uppercase or traversal IDs as InvalidRequest; the reads change no store file; a second Host on the same store returns the same records. Hosts on tampered copies refuse an edited earlier revision and a missing revision as JournalInvalid and an altered admission response as ArtifactChanged.
limitations: The records come from native runs curated separately; this run reads them through the Host on copies and starts no TIA, worker or PLCSIM. Live reads during a native workflow are the 14 the watch runs recorded.
Watch operations cover one existing-row Bool ModifyValue and watch authoring; other native families keep only dispatch admissions (change_apply, change_restore, scratch_create).
Cooperating Hosts share one local artifact store; a remote or network store is not exercised.
